text:
tasha: Hey team, first-week question. I accepted the org invite but when I open github.com/orgs/redwood-inference it shows my account twice (one labeled as an enterprise account). When I try to push to a private repo I get 403. SSO flow also complained about "account managed by organization" and wouldn't finish. Who should I ping? cc @leo

leo: welcome! can you paste the git push error and which GitHub username shows in the invite email? Also did you accept using a personal or work GitHub account?

tasha: Invite email shows `tasha.dev` and I accepted from that. My work account is `tasha-work` though — I thought they were linked. Push error is:
```
$ git push origin feature/x
remote: Permission to redwood-inference/app.git denied to tasha-personal.
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/app.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403
```

it-support: sounds like the repo sees `tasha-personal` as the actor. The double-account UI can happen when a user has a personal account invited before the org was under an enterprise SAML domain, then later the enterprise claim links emails. SSO enforcement may be blocking the personal account. Run `gh api user` and `gh api orgs/redwood-inference/memberships/tasha-personal` (or tasha-work) and paste outputs.

tasha: `gh api user` returns my local auth user as `tasha-personal`. I think my local GH CLI credentials are for the wrong account.

onboarding-bot: Reminder: If you have multiple GitHub accounts, accept invites with the account you intend to use for work. For enterprise SSO, the enterprise account must complete SSO before you get member access.

leo: two paths: 1) re-send invite to `tasha-work` and have you accept that, then update local auth to `tasha-work`; or 2) convert `tasha-personal` into the enterprise-managed account by verifying the org email and completing SSO, but that might merge enterprise control onto that username. Which do you prefer?

tasha: I want to keep personal separate. Please re-invite `tasha-work`.

it-support: re-sent invite to `tasha-work`. Meanwhile to avoid local creds confusing pushes, run:
```
# clear cached https token
git credential-osxkeychain erase
# or clear gh auth and re-login
gh auth logout --hostname github.com && gh auth login
```
This will prompt you to authenticate as `tasha-work` when you login. If you use SSH, ensure your SSH key maps to the correct account (`ssh -T git@github.com`).

tasha: re-logged in and accepted invite as `tasha-work`. SSO flow still showed the enterprise banner but completed after I verified the org email. I had to remove the cached token and re-run `gh auth login` to pick the correct account.

security: note: once SSO is enforced you must use the org-managed account for code pushes to private repos. Personal accounts may remain personal but will be blocked from org resources until SSO is completed.

it-support: I converted your membership from outside collaborator to member now that `tasha-work` completed SSO. Try a push now.

tasha: push succeeded! thanks all. Two small onboarding notes: 1) add a line in the onboarding doc about re-logging `gh auth` if you switch accounts, 2) mention enterprise-linked emails creating duplicate UI entries so folks don't panic.

leo: good call. Filing a doc update. Glad you're onboarded — welcome! :tada:

it-support: resolved and closing thread. :white_check_mark:
